problem.title: What Must Come Next?
problem.statement: A sequence begins 1, 2, 4. With no rule stated, which next term is guaranteed?
hints: Try writing two different rules that both begin 1, 2, 4.
A prefix is evidence about a rule, not the rule itself.

solutionSteps.title: Build one valid rule
solutionSteps.body: If each term doubles, the next term is 8.

solutionSteps.title: Build another
solutionSteps.body: If the increases are +1, +2, +3, then the next term is 7. Both rules fit 1, 2, 4, so no next term is guaranteed.

validationMethods: constructive non-uniqueness: doubling gives next term 8 while successive increases +1,+2,+3 give next term 7
independent third construction: a_n = 2^(n-1) + (n-1)(n-2)(n-3)/6 begins 1,2,4 but has fourth term 9, so no numerical choice is logically guaranteed

problem.title: Twelfth Term
problem.statement: The arithmetic sequence 7, 11, 15, 19, ... continues with constant difference 4. What is its 12th term?
hints: From term 1 to term 12 there are 11 equal steps.
Do not confuse the term number 12 with its value.

solutionSteps.title: Count the gaps
solutionSteps.body: There are 12 - 1 = 11 increases from the first term to the twelfth.

validationMethods: independent recursive extension and option audit: eleven additions of 4 to 7 reach 51, the unique listed result

problem.title: Follow the Previous Term
problem.statement: A sequence has first term 2. Every later term is 3 more than the previous term. What is the sixth term?
hints: Write one new term at a time.
The first term is already counted; reaching the sixth takes five additions.

solutionSteps.title: Separate index and value
solutionSteps.body: The card labeled term 6 carries value 17.

validationMethods: independent explicit translation a_n = 2 + 3(n - 1) gives a_6 = 17; choices audited

problem.title: Use the Position
problem.statement: A sequence is defined explicitly by a_n = 3n - 2. What is a_15?
hints: In a_15, the term index is n = 15.
Substitute the index into the explicit rule.

validationMethods: independent arithmetic-sequence check: terms begin 1,4,7 and fourteen steps of 3 from term 1 give 1 + 42 = 43; options audited

problem.title: Double, Then Add One
problem.statement: A sequence starts with 1. Each later term is one more than twice the previous term. What is the sixth term?
hints: Apply both parts of the rule to one term at a time.
Check whether the differences stay constant before calling it arithmetic.

validationMethods: independent closed-form observation a_n = 2^n - 1 gives a_6 = 63; all choices audited

problem.title: Hundredth Tile
problem.statement: Tiles repeat in the order red, blue, green, red, blue, green, and so on. What color is the 100th tile?

choices.label: D
choices.text: It could be red or blue

hints: The pattern has a cycle of length 3.

solutionSteps.title: Locate the cycle
solutionSteps.body: Since 99 is divisible by 3, tile 99 is the third position in a cycle, green.

solutionSteps.title: Move one step
solutionSteps.body: Tile 100 starts the next cycle, so it is red.

validationMethods: division algorithm: 100 = 3(33) + 1, so position 100 has cycle position 1, red
independent neighbor check: position 99 completes 33 full red-blue-green cycles, making the next tile red; options audited
